hpi: {{patient_name}} is a young woman with recent appendectomy who presents to the inpatient unit with RLQ abdominal pain, fever, tachycardia, nausea, and vomiting. She is febrile and tachycardic with localized RLQ tenderness. Labs show leukocytosis. The combination of recent abdominal surgery, fever, tachycardia, and localized pain is highly suggestive of a postoperative intra-abdominal abscess. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast is the imaging of choice. Management involves percutaneous image-guided abscess drainage (first-line, avoiding the morbidity of open laparotomy) plus broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics covering gram-negative organisms, anaerobes, and enterococci.
